answer:
1. The animation shows a historical comparison of buying and renting in the US. It uses a grid with one cell for every possible start month from January 1991 to July 2016. Each start month is followed for ten years. The data sources named are FHFA home prices, BLS rents and Freddie Mac mortgage rates. All of it is labeled "illustrative."

2. The grid of flat tiles turns into a perspective view of rows of small houses, so each start month becomes its own house. In the last two frames the view narrows to a single character, Nina, standing between an apartment building and a house. The apartment building has a small rent sign on it. In frame 6 a second figure stands beside Nina at the house.

3. It means the answer to "rent or buy?" depends on when you started. Each house is a separate ten-year outcome, so the picture is about the spread of outcomes across many start dates, not one average result. Nina is a single example drawn from that spread.

4. The animation gives no advice. The on-screen text says "Not advice on whether to buy or rent" and "US only · history, not a forecast." A viewer should take away only that outcomes varied by start date and that the past doesn't predict the future. The frames don't show which option cost more.

5. The advice in 4 comes from the animation's own text. It is not my conclusion. The disclaimers say it is not advice and not a forecast. My reading that outcomes depend on start date is an inference from the grid of start months, and the frames don't state it outright.
